maya: quick summary — ran continuous-batcher sweep across us-west1 (A100) and eu-west1 (H100). Variables: batch_window {25,50,100} ms, max_batch_tokens {512,1024,2048}, kernel choices: flash_attn / cutlass / triton, quant: bf16 vs int8.

ben: can you paste the p50/p95 and throughput numbers?

maya: sure — high-level table (tokens/sec = aggregate tokens produced per second for generation workload):
```
GPU   | region   | batch_window | max_batch_tokens | kernel      | quant  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | tokens/sec
A100  | us-west1 | 25 ms        | 2048             | flash_attn  | bf16   | 46      | 160     | 37000
A100  | us-west1 | 50 ms        | 2048             | flash_attn  | bf16   | 58      | 210     | 44000
A100  | us-west1 | 25 ms        | 1024             | cutlass     | int8   | 52      | 175     | 41000
H100  | eu-west1 | 25 ms        | 2048             | triton      | bf16   | 42      | 150     | 49000
H100  | eu-west1 | 50 ms        | 2048             | triton      | int8   | 55      | 260     | 62000
H100  | eu-west1 | 100 ms       | 2048             | triton      | int8   | 90      | 430     | 68000
```
Notes: int8 increases tokens/sec but p95 jumps in cross-tenant (eu-west) runs when batch_window >=50ms.

liam: nice. how did you run the harness? config + command please.

maya: command I used: `./bench/runner --model=rw-infer-v1 --region=eu-west1 --gpu=h100 --batch-window-ms=50 --max-batch-tokens=2048 --kernel=triton --quant=int8 --duration=900`
Scheduler snippet I tested (pasted inline):
```
{
  "scheduler": "continuous",
  "batch_window_ms": 50,
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
  "fairness": {
    "mode": "tenant_share",
    "max_wait_ms": 250,
    "priority_weights": {"interactive": 1.6, "background": 0.8}
  },
  "kernel_preference": ["triton","cutlass","flash_attn"]
}
```
ops-bot: deployed continuous-scheduler v2 to canary (eng-ml-canary) :rocket:

eva: saw tail spikes in eu-west with 50ms window — could be KV cache invalidation/release causing serialization across microbatches?

maya: yup. cache hit-rate dropped ~8% at higher windows because slightly staler KV shards triggered refill. That made bigger batches wait for KV pulls -> higher p95. Logs show repeated `kv_fetch` on hot prefixes around p95 windows.

ben: recommendation?

maya: short list:
- For latency-sensitive interactive loads: prefer H100 w/ batch_window 25–30ms, max_batch_tokens <=1024, prefer bf16 or int8 with conservative kernels (triton fallback to flash_attn).
- For throughput-max use-cases: H100 + int8 + batch_window 50–100ms, but add backpressure rules per-tenant to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Scheduler change: enforce `max_wait_ms` (200–300ms) and `tenant_share` fairness so one noisy tenant doesn't fill large batches.
- Ops: increase KV prefetch concurrency and instrument per-prefix latency + hit-rate.

liam: can you upload raw CSVs/plots to the perf bucket? I'll run a 12h stress sweep with different priority mixes.

maya: uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/eng-ml/cont-batcher/1759123456/ — csv + p99/throughput charts + run configs. ping me if you need access.

ben: thanks — can you open a small RFC for the scheduler weight defaults? want to iterate quickly before next deploy.

maya: will do — I'll draft RFC with test plan and suggested defaults (attach perf artifacts).

ops-bot: incident-note: no customer impact observed during canary.

eva: tagging @maya for follow-up on KV tuning :+1:

maya: noted — follow-up tomorrow, will include mitigations and a short test to verify cache hit-rate improves with proposed prefetch knobs.
